transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date: 2026-06-30
Start: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Liam Brooks (Redwood CSM), Ava Summers (Citrine Head of ML), Diego Ramos (Citrine Platform Eng), Priya Nair (Citrine Data Privacy), Tom Kwan (Citrine Product)

AUTO SUMMARY (auto): Weekly POC check-in. Focus: scorecard regressions, prompt fixes, plan rollback drill, staging access + security questions.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick roll call, we got the same crew?
[00:06] Ava (Citrine): Yep, hi all, Ava here.
[00:08] Diego (Citrine): Diego, on platform.
[00:10] Priya (Citrine): Priya, privacy.
[00:12] Raj (Redwood SE): Raj here, ready to dig in.
[00:15] Tom (Citrine): Tom, product.
[00:17] Maya: Cool. Agenda: one, review the scorecard diffs since last deploy; two, triage the two high-sev fails on the NER prompt set; three, plan rollback rehearsal; four, security/staging access. Anything to add?
[00:28] Ava: That's it. Also we wanted to hear options for dedicated vs hosted for the POC if regressions persist, uh, because of cost concerns.
[00:36] Maya: Yep, we'll cover that in the tradeoffs section.

[00:45] Raj: Okay jumping in — we pulled the latest scorecard. There's a 3.8% drop on the entity extraction precision on the clinical prompts, most of the failures are short-form lab results where the model hallucinates units. We flagged two sample examples as high severity.
[00:58] [01:02] Raj: Example one, input: "Patient labs: sodium 139, potassium 4.2" output mapped potassium as mmol/L when that wasn't present in the prompt, so extraneous unit.
[01:12] Priya: That one is a privacy risk because downstream parsers rely on units for PHI handling, so it's causing mis-routes in the pipeline.
[01:19] Maya: Got it. Did we see any correlation to sequence length or the quantized runner?
[01:24] Raj: There's a slight signal — the failures skew to shorter sequences and the 4-bit quant path. But not conclusive; we need a controlled sweep.
[01:32] Diego: Are you seeing any infra-related TTL or KV caching artifacts? Could K V cash be serving stale prefixes?
[01:38] Raj: Good question. We looked at prefix cache hit rates — not high enough to explain these false units. Might be model behavior. Also note we rolled a small tokenizer tweak in the last deploy, that could shift decode probabilities.
[01:49] Ava: Ok so probably model + tokenizer. What's the quick mitigation?
[01:52] Maya: Two prongs: one, patch the prompt to explicitly include a small guardrail that says "do not invent units; only repeat units if present" — minimal-cost approach. Two, if that fails, we fallback to a more conservative model variant with higher token-respect but higher cost.
[02:05] Tom: How much higher?
[02:07] Maya: Rough estimate — about 25% cost delta; latency improves slightly on the quantized variant but precision drops. So it's a tradeoff.
[02:15] [02:20] Priya: From compliance angle we also want to log raw responses for forensics but redact PII; can we provide logs with PII token pointers instead of full text?
[02:29] Raj: We can capture token-level traces and then run a redaction pass. Redwood's platform supports KMS-encrypted logs and audit trails, and we can tie to your HSM if needed. Note: log retention and export need policy signoff.
[02:43] Priya: OK please send the exact retention policy snippets.

[02:50] Maya: On the rollback drill — propose we rehearse a canary rollback in staging: step 1, push patch prompts to staging; step 2, run 1k sample sweep; step 3, if scorecard passes thresholds, promote; if not, rollback model routing to previous variant and capture metrics.
[03:06] Diego: We'll need staging VPC creds for the routing test and to capture perf metrics in our telemetry.
[03:11] Raj: We'll also run a latency/throughput bench on the candidate variant — quant vs fp16 — and share the CSV.
[03:17] [03:22] Ava: Can you quantify the expected time for a rollback? We want to coordinate with on-call.
[03:25] Raj: Warm routing rollback is typically <3 minutes if caches are cold; with Kv cache invalidation it can be up to 7–10 minutes, depending on outstanding sessions. We'll script the invalidation.
[03:36] Tom: Who's on the rollback runbook?
[03:39] Maya: Proposed: Maya (AE) coordinates play, Raj runs infra commands, Diego toggles routing in staging, Ava signs off on quality gate, Priya monitors data/privacy constraints. Liam will run the postmortem notes.

[03:50] [04:00] Diego: Quick question — for the staging VPC, we need cross-account peering and a one-time IAM role. Diego: I'll send a network diagram.
[04:07] Maya: Perfect. Include sample log paths and where to put the shared CSV. We prefer the shared drive link: https://rwd-internal.example/po c-results (note: link readout may be truncated).

[04:20] Raj: Back to the prompt fixes — we tried a soft-prompt addition and a negative example in the few-shot context. The patched prompts cut that failure class by ~60% on small bench but introduced a small drop in recall for edge-case abbreviations.
[04:32] Ava: Hmm, we can't lose recall on abbreviations — clinical abbreviations are crucial.
[04:35] Raj: Understood. We'll craft a targeted prompt that preserves abbreviations: add a short instruction block like "preserve abbreviations exactly as shown" plus an explicit negative example for hallucinated units.
[04:45] Maya: We'll iterate on that and share the patched set.

[04:52] [05:05] Priya: Security question — does Redwood Dedicated support S S O integration with our Okta and SAML, and can we enforce RBAC on route-level logs?
[05:13] Maya: Yes, Redwood Dedicated supports SAML/Okta SSO and per-token RBAC. Audit logs can be scoped by route and model. For Private deployments we have options for customer-managed KMS/HSM and retention policies.
[05:23] Priya: Great. Please attach the SOC 2 Type II report and the KMS integration guide.
[05:28] Maya: Will do — I'll share the security pack after the call.

[05:35] Raj: Also flag — we noticed one odd sample where the model reversed the patient gender in the summary. Could be dataset bias or a prompt framing issue. We added it to the safety ticket.
[05:45] Ava: That's high severity, please prioritize.
[05:47] Raj: Yep.

[05:50] [06:00] Maya: Ok rolling into timeline: we'll push patched prompts to staging tomorrow (2026-07-01), Raj will run the 1k regression sweep on 2026-07-02, Diego to provide VPC creds by 2026-07-01, and we'll run rollback drill on 2026-07-07.
[06:13] Tom: For the 1k sweep, what's the pass threshold?
[06:16] Raj: Pass = no worse than baseline on precision/recall delta of 1.5% and no high-severity failures in the sample.
[06:23] Priya: And retention for logs? We need 90 days for audit but redacted versions should live longer.
[06:28] Diego: We can export to our compliance bucket, but need the redaction contract.

[06:35] Maya: Any competitor concerns? Ava mentioned Anthropic for safety-first models; we noted some customers use Anthropic for stricter hallucination control but pay a premium.
[06:45] Ava: We're keeping an open mind; your observability is a strong point.

[06:50] [07:00] Liam (Redwood CSM): I'll put together the playbook doc for the rollback and the postmortem template; will share a calendar invite for the drill.
[07:06] Maya: Great. Any other questions?
[07:09] Priya: One last — can we get a sample of token-level logs redacted for PII to review before we accept retention?
[07:16] Raj: Yes, we'll produce a sanitized sample.

[07:20] Maya: Alright, recap: patched prompts + scoring CSV (Maya) by 2026-07-03; 1k sweep (Raj) by 2026-07-02; staging creds (Diego) by 2026-07-01; rollback drill scheduled 2026-07-07; security pack (Maya) w SOC2/KMS docs.
[07:36] Ava: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:39] Tom: Thanks.
[07:40] Maya: Thanks team, talk soon.
[07:43] [07:52] End of recording.

ATTACHMENTS/REFERENCES: "Patch prompts v1" (link in shared drive), "scorecard-diff-june30.csv" (drive), security-pack.pdf (SOC2, KMS guide).

NOTES: Transcript contains occasional transcription artifacts ("K V cash" instead of KV cache, S S O for SSO). Speaker labels automated.
